raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

On ROCm, each DeepSeek V4.1 mHC seam ran the whole fused AITER kernel pair on the default stream before the next sublayer could start. That pair is the post block, the gate projection, Sinkhorn, and the collapse with RMSNorm. This PR moves the gate projection onto a side stream inside FULL HIP graphs, so it overlaps with the following attention or FFN. The default stream now only runs the post block plus the RMSNorm'd collapse, in one new Triton kernel. This is the ROCm counterpart of the CUDA overlap in [#57603](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57603).

## Claims

- Output throughput is up 0.3% to 5.4% end to end on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, EP, FP8 KV, MI355X, at every concurrency from 1 to 128 at TP2, TP4 and TP8.
- The new residual and the gates (post, comb, next pre) are bit-identical to the fused AITER seam. The layer input is bit-identical up to 16 tokens and within one bf16 ulp above that.
- No change outside FULL-graph decode with at most 128 tokens. Prefill, piecewise graphs, eager mode, CUDA and DSpark draft layers keep the current path.



## Validation



### Kernel

MI355X, HIP-graph replay time per seam. "Fused" is `mhc_fused_post_pre_delayed_rms_norm_aiter` (main + reduce kernels). "Input kernel" is the new `mhc_post_collapse_rms_norm_triton`, the only part left on the default stream. "Gates" is the side-stream work.


| tokens | fused (µs) | input kernel (µs) | gates on side stream (µs) |
| ------ | ---------- | ----------------- | ------------------------- |
| 1      | 9.91       | 4.15              | 8.48                      |
| 4      | 10.24      | 4.26              | 9.01                      |
| 16     | 10.41      | 4.37              | 9.17                      |


The default-stream seam goes from about 10 µs to about 4.3 µs. That is roughly 0.5 ms per decode step across the 86 seams that take the overlap (43 layers × 2).

### End-to-end

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on MI355X, TP4, EP, FP8 KV, 12 sweep points. Mean TPOT in ms and output throughput in tok/s:


| input / output | concurrency | TPOT main | TPOT this PR | Δ     | tok/s main | tok/s this PR | Δ     |
| -------------- | ----------- | --------- | ------------ | ----- | ---------- | ------------- | ----- |
| 8192 / 1024    | 4           | 8.08      | 7.70         | -4.8% | 466.71     | 488.68        | +4.7% |
| 8192 / 1024    | 8           | 9.80      | 9.46         | -3.5% | 773.17     | 799.60        | +3.4% |
| 8192 / 1024    | 16          | 11.84     | 11.50        | -2.9% | 1262.50    | 1300.66       | +3.0% |
| 8192 / 1024    | 32          | 16.12     | 15.69        | -2.7% | 1786.03    | 1833.31       | +2.6% |
| 8192 / 1024    | 64          | 23.14     | 22.90        | -1.1% | 2516.82    | 2539.97       | +0.9% |
| 8192 / 1024    | 128         | 35.31     | 34.51        | -2.3% | 3161.18    | 3225.27       | +2.0% |
| 8192 / 1024    | 256         | 58.27     | 57.96        | -0.5% | 3795.31    | 3815.37       | +0.5% |
| 60000 / 600    | 4           | 13.80     | 13.47        | -2.4% | 227.83     | 233.61        | +2.5% |
| 60000 / 600    | 16          | 39.88     | 39.98        | +0.2% | 337.21     | 338.35        | +0.3% |
| 60000 / 600    | 64          | 138.79    | 136.17       | -1.9% | 388.60     | 394.46        | +1.5% |
| 128000 / 1024  | 4           | 16.85     | 16.53        | -1.9% | 185.12     | 187.66        | +1.4% |
| 128000 / 1024  | 16          | 54.22     | 53.73        | -0.9% | 247.55     | 250.08        | +1.0% |


The mean is -2.05% TPOT and +2.00% throughput. Throughput is higher at all 12 points and TPOT lower at 11; the exception is 60000 / 600 at concurrency 16, at +0.2%. Median TPOT gives -2.14%, also 11 of 12, so the whole distribution moves rather than a tail.

### Accuracy

GSM8K, 5-shot, `lm_eval` `local-completions`, full test split, `num_concurrent=32`:


| run     | flexible-extract | strict-match    |
| ------- | ---------------- | --------------- |
| default | 0.9227 ± 0.0074  | 0.9219 ± 0.0074 |
| this PR | 0.9234 ± 0.0073  | 0.9234 ± 0.0073 |


### Tests

```bash
pytest tests/kernels/mhc/test_mhc_kernels.py -k rocm
```

All pass on MI355X. `test_deepseek_v41_rocm_mhc_overlap_matches_fused_seam` is new and runs at 1, 2, 7, 16, 64 and 128 tokens. After joining the side stream, it compares every output with `MHCPreDelayedOp.forward_hip` (the fused AITER seam):

- the residual and gates must match exactly;
- the layer input must match within one bf16 ulp, and it must already be usable before the join;
- the same checks are repeated across three HIP-graph replays with changing inputs.

CI runs it in `:amd: (MI355) mHC Kernels`.

## Details

**Why the split is exact.** In AITER's fused seam (`_mhc_fused_post_pre_delayed_rmsnorm_main_kernel`), the post-mix is rounded to bf16 once, and that rounded `R'` feeds the projection, the square sums and the collapse. This PR splits the seam in two:

- The new kernel recomputes `R'` with the same expression order, so it is bit-identical, then collapses it with the carried pre-mix and applies the RMSNorm.
- The side stream runs AITER's own fused kernel on `R'` without the post (`HAS_POST=False`). Its gates are therefore the same numbers.

Only the RMSNorm's row sum differs. The new kernel holds a token's row in registers and sums it in one pass, while AITER reduces it across split-K programs, so the order changes. That is exact at decode sizes, and within one ulp otherwise.

**Gating.** The overlap runs only inside FULL HIP-graph capture, not in piecewise graphs, with `0 < tokens <= MHC_OVERLAP_MAX_TOKENS` (128). Fork and join then become graph edges; `DeepseekV41ROCMAiterMLAAttention` keeps its aux streams to captured graphs for the same reason. It also requires AITER's fused delayed seam (`HAS_AITER_MHC_FUSED_POST_PRE_DELAYED_RMS_NORM`), `hc_mult == 4`, and no ubatching. The 128-token limit is the largest tested point. The gain was still positive there but shrinking (above), and the overlap was not measured beyond it, although FULL graphs go up to 512 tokens.

**Seams.** The overlap applies to every FFN seam and to the attention seam of every layer after the first. Layer 0's broadcast seam and Engram seams already take a different path and keep it. The gate stream is joined after attention and at the end of each layer, which is where the gates are next read. The stream is separate from the attention aux streams, as on CUDA. `record_stream` keeps the side stream's inputs and the main stream's gate outputs alive across the fork. No host synchronization is added.

**Limitations.**

- **Tuning:** the token limit was tuned on MI355X TP2, TP4 and TP8.



### Existing PRs

I searched vllm-project/vllm PRs (open and closed) for mHC overlap, coefficient and side-stream work on ROCm. None moves the mHC seam off the default stream on ROCm.

- [#57603](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57603) (merged) is the CUDA version. It needs SM100 and DeepGEMM's `tf32_hc_prenorm_gemm`, and stops at 16 tokens. This PR follows its structure, gating and join points.
- [#56853](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56853) (merged) adds an attention-side aux stream for DeepSeek-V4 HCA layers. It keeps the mHC seam serial on the default stream, which is what this PR changes.
- [#58655](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58655) (merged) introduced the fused AITER delayed seam that this PR splits.


---

<summary> Pull Request Checklist </summary>

- [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans).
- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.

- [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity.
- [x] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI.
- [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples.
- [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.
</details>

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

Before approving this, can we either gate the overlap to gfx950 or add gfx942 validation? supports_mhc_overlap() currently enables the path on any ROCm target where the AITER operation is available, but the validation and the 128-token limit are based only on MI355X.
Great work! Can we please do some checks if this also works with dcp and sequence parallel and similar?

**Minor**: is it possible to simplify this a bit by following the structure used in the nvidia/model? I.e.

```
        mhc_pre = (
            partial(mhc_pre_delayed_overlap, stream=mhc_stream)
            if mhc_stream is not None
            else mhc_pre_delayed_tilelang
        )
```

and call mhc_pre unconditionally

**Nit question**: I kind of like the name mhc_pre_delayed_overlap more than mhc_seam_overlap, WDYT?

**Suggestion**: can we check fi we need to register this new kernel for warmup?

 One can run with `--jit-monitor-mode error` to check this

**Question**: can we check if there's a risk we're breaking things given the condition is slightly different from where we sync below (there we just check if the aux stream exists)? I.e. can we get a situation where mhc_stream exist but pre_mix be None? If so we would not run in two streams, but we'd still wait on the aux stream after the ffn

**Question**: I think this will bypass the check of if the aiter mhc kernel is supported by calling it this way (i.e. never checking `_aiter_mhc_supported`). I'm thinking if we should call the MHCPreDelayedOp instead which does this checking for us. Can you check this please?
**Minor**: If we want I think we could re-use enable_multi_stream_overlap utility here

**Optional question**: I might be completely wrong here, but is the norm done in this kernel and the norm done in `mhc_fused_post_pre_delayed_rms_norm_aiter` both on the layer input (i.e. partly redundant) or is it norming different things? Thinking if a natural follow up optimization is to get rid of that if that's the case
**Small question**: What's the reason for 0 absolute tolerance here? I'm thinking if we rather should add a small value if this will always lead to a pass if one of the elements are exactly 0

@@ -1389,6 +1389,67 @@ def test_mhc_pre_delayed_rocm_aiter_fused_rms_norm(num_tokens, seam):
     torch.testing.assert_close(actual[2], expected_layer_input, atol=2e-2, rtol=1e-2)
 
 
+@pytest.mark.skipif(
+    not (current_platform.is_rocm() and HAS_AITER_MHC_FUSED_POST_PRE_DELAYED_RMS_NORM),
+    reason="AITER fused delayed-seam kernel required (gfx950)",
+)
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("num_tokens", [1, 2, 7, 16, 64, 128])
+def test_deepseek_v41_rocm_mhc_overlap_matches_fused_seam(num_tokens):
+    """Moving the gate projection to a side stream keeps the residual and gates
+    bit-exact and the layer input within one bf16 ulp, and the layer input is
+    usable before the join; also across graph replays."""
+    from vllm.models.deepseek_v41.amd.mhc import mhc_seam_overlap
+
+    set_random_seed(0)
+    hc_mult, hidden_size = 4, 5120
+    residual, fn, hc_scale, hc_base, norm_weight = _rocm_mhc_inputs(
+        num_tokens=num_tokens, hidden_size=hidden_size, hc_mult=hc_mult
+    )
+    sublayer_out = torch.randn(
+        num_tokens, hidden_size, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device=DEVICE
+    )
+    post_layer_mix = 2 * torch.rand(num_tokens, hc_mult, 1, device=DEVICE)
+    comb_res_mix = torch.softmax(
+        torch.randn(num_tokens, hc_mult, hc_mult, device=DEVICE), dim=-1
+    )
+    pre_mix = torch.rand(num_tokens, hc_mult, device=DEVICE) + 0.5
+    args = (residual, fn, hc_scale, hc_base, 1e-6, 1e-6, 1e-6, 2.0, 20)
+    kwargs = dict(
+        pre_mix=pre_mix,
+        sublayer_out=sublayer_out,
+        post_layer_mix=post_layer_mix,
+        comb_res_mix=comb_res_mix,
+        norm_weight=norm_weight,
+        norm_eps=1e-6,
+    )
+    side = torch.cuda.Stream()
+
+    def run():
+        outputs = mhc_seam_overlap(*args, **kwargs, stream=side)
+        consumed_input = outputs[3].clone()
+        torch.cuda.current_stream().wait_stream(side)
+        return (*outputs, consumed_input)
+
+    def check(actual):
+        expected = object.__new__(MHCPreDelayedOp).forward_hip(*args, **kwargs)
+        for i in (0, 1, 2, 4):
+            torch.testing.assert_close(actual[i], expected[i], atol=0, rtol=0)
+        # The RMSNorm row sum is reduced in another order than AITER's split-K.
+        for layer_input in (actual[3], actual[5]):
+            torch.testing.assert_close(layer_input, expected[3], atol=0, rtol=2**-7)
+
+    check(run())
+    graph = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
+    with torch.cuda.graph(graph):
+        captured = run()
+    for _ in range(3):
+        for tensor in (residual, sublayer_out):
+            tensor.normal_()
+        pre_mix.uniform_(0.5, 1.5)
+        graph.replay()
+        check(captured)
+
+
 @pytest.mark.skipif(
     not (current_platform.is_rocm() and HAS_AITER_MHC),
     reason="AITER mHC required",

@@ -141,6 +141,116 @@ def _hc_collapse_triton_fake(x: Tensor, pre_mix: Tensor) -> Tensor:
     return torch.empty(x.shape[0], x.shape[2], dtype=x.dtype, device=x.device)
 
 
+@triton.jit
+def _mhc_post_stream(post_mix_ptr, comb_mix_ptr, t, j, xt, f0, f1, f2, f3):
+    comb = comb_mix_ptr + t * 16 + j  # comb is [source h, destination j]
+    return (
+        tl.load(post_mix_ptr + t * 4 + j) * xt
+        + tl.load(comb) * f0
+        + tl.load(comb + 4) * f1
+        + tl.load(comb + 8) * f2
+        + tl.load(comb + 12) * f3
+    ).to(tl.bfloat16)
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _mhc_post_collapse_rms_norm_kernel(
+    residual_ptr,
+    x_ptr,
+    post_mix_ptr,
+    comb_mix_ptr,
+    pre_mix_ptr,
+    weight_ptr,
+    residual_out_ptr,
+    out_ptr,
+    norm_eps,
+    H: tl.constexpr,
+    BLOCK_H: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    """One token per program. The post-mix and collapse keep the expression
+    order of aiter's ``_mhc_fused_post_pre_delayed_rmsnorm_main_kernel``, so the
+    new residual is bit-identical to it."""
+    t = tl.program_id(0).to(tl.int64)
+    cols = tl.arange(0, BLOCK_H)
+    mask = cols < H
+    res = residual_ptr + t * 4 * H + cols
+    f0 = tl.load(res, mask=mask, other=0.0).to(tl.float32)
+    f1 = tl.load(res + H, mask=mask, other=0.0).to(tl.float32)
+    f2 = tl.load(res + 2 * H, mask=mask, other=0.0).to(tl.float32)
+    f3 = tl.load(res + 3 * H, mask=mask, other=0.0).to(tl.float32)
+    xt = tl.load(x_ptr + t * H + cols, mask=mask, other=0.0).to(tl.float32)
+    g0 = _mhc_post_stream(post_mix_ptr, comb_mix_ptr, t, 0, xt, f0, f1, f2, f3)
+    g1 = _mhc_post_stream(post_mix_ptr, comb_mix_ptr, t, 1, xt, f0, f1, f2, f3)
+    g2 = _mhc_post_stream(post_mix_ptr, comb_mix_ptr, t, 2, xt, f0, f1, f2, f3)
+    g3 = _mhc_post_stream(post_mix_ptr, comb_mix_ptr, t, 3, xt, f0, f1, f2, f3)
+    out_res = residual_out_ptr + t * 4 * H + cols
+    tl.store(out_res, g0, mask=mask)
+    tl.store(out_res + H, g1, mask=mask)
+    tl.store(out_res + 2 * H, g2, mask=mask)
+    tl.store(out_res + 3 * H, g3, mask=mask)
+    pre = pre_mix_ptr + t * 4
+    x1 = (
+        tl.load(pre) * g0.to(tl.float32)
+        + tl.load(pre + 1) * g1.to(tl.float32)
+        + tl.load(pre + 2) * g2.to(tl.float32)
+        + tl.load(pre + 3) * g3.to(tl.float32)
+    ).to(tl.bfloat16)
+    x1f = x1.to(tl.float32)
+    rstd = tl.math.rsqrt(tl.sum(x1f * x1f, 0) * (1.0 / H) + norm_eps)
+    w = tl.load(weight_ptr + cols, mask=mask, other=0.0).to(tl.float32)
+    tl.store(out_ptr + t * H + cols, ((x1f * rstd) * w).to(tl.bfloat16), mask=mask)
+
+
+def mhc_post_collapse_rms_norm_triton(
+    residual: Tensor,
+    sublayer_out: Tensor,
+    post_layer_mix: Tensor,
+    comb_res_mix: Tensor,
+    pre_mix: Tensor,
+    norm_weight: Tensor,
+    norm_eps: float,
+) -> tuple[Tensor, Tensor]:
+    """The layer-input half of a delayed mHC seam, without the gate projection.
+
+    Applies the post block and returns the new residual and the RMSNorm of its
+    collapse with the carried ``pre_mix``, which is what
+    ``mhc_fused_post_pre_delayed_rms_norm_aiter`` returns besides the gates.
+
+    Args:
+        residual: [T, 4, H] bf16 residual streams entering the seam.
+        sublayer_out: [T, H] bf16 output of the sublayer before the seam.
+        post_layer_mix: [T, 4, 1] fp32 post gate of the previous seam.
+        comb_res_mix: [T, 4, 4] fp32 residual comb of the previous seam.
+        pre_mix: [T, 4] fp32 pre gate carried from the previous seam.
+        norm_weight: [H] RMSNorm weight.
+        norm_eps: RMSNorm epsilon.
+
+    Returns:
+        The [T, 4, H] bf16 new residual and the [T, H] bf16 layer input.
+
+    """
+    T, hc_mult, H = residual.shape
+    assert hc_mult == 4 and residual.dtype == torch.bfloat16
+    residual_out = torch.empty_like(residual)
+    out = torch.empty(T, H, dtype=residual.dtype, device=residual.device)
+    if T:
+        _mhc_post_collapse_rms_norm_kernel[(T,)](
+            residual.contiguous(),
+            sublayer_out.contiguous(),
+            post_layer_mix.contiguous(),
+            comb_res_mix.contiguous(),
+            pre_mix.contiguous(),
+            norm_weight,
+            residual_out,
+            out,
+            norm_eps,
+            H=H,
+            BLOCK_H=triton.next_power_of_2(H),
+            num_warps=16,
+        )
+    return residual_out, out

+"""Overlap the DSV4.1 mHC gate projection with the next sublayer on ROCm."""
+
+import torch
+
+from vllm.config import VllmConfig
+from vllm.model_executor.kernels.mhc.triton import mhc_post_collapse_rms_norm_triton
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.mhc import (
+    HAS_AITER_MHC_FUSED_POST_PRE_DELAYED_RMS_NORM,
+)
+from vllm.platforms import current_platform
+
+# MI355X TP4 improves through 128 tokens, shrinking from +5% output throughput
+# at 1 token to +1.7% at 128.
+MHC_OVERLAP_MAX_TOKENS = 128
+
+
+def supports_mhc_overlap(vllm_config: VllmConfig) -> bool:
+    config = vllm_config.model_config.hf_config
+    return (
+        current_platform.is_rocm()
+        and HAS_AITER_MHC_FUSED_POST_PRE_DELAYED_RMS_NORM
+        and config.hc_mult == 4
+        and not vllm_config.parallel_config.use_ubatching
+    )
+
+
+def mhc_seam_overlap(
+    residual: torch.Tensor,
+    fn: torch.Tensor,
+    hc_scale: torch.Tensor,
+    hc_base: torch.Tensor,
+    rms_eps: float,
+    hc_pre_eps: float,
+    hc_sinkhorn_eps: float,
+    hc_post_mult_value: float,
+    sinkhorn_repeat: int,
+    *,
+    pre_mix: torch.Tensor,
+    sublayer_out: torch.Tensor,
+    post_layer_mix: torch.Tensor,
+    comb_res_mix: torch.Tensor,
+    norm_weight: torch.Tensor,
+    norm_eps: float,
+    stream: torch.cuda.Stream,
+) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
+    """``MHCPreDelayedOp`` with the gate projection moved onto ``stream``.
+
+    Returns residual, post_mix, comb_mix, layer_input, next_pre_mix. Only the
+    residual and layer input are ready on the caller stream; join ``stream``
+    before using the gates. The residual and gates match the fused AITER seam
+    bit for bit, since the gates are AITER's kernel applied to the same new
+    residual; the layer input's RMSNorm sums its row in another order, which
+    can move it by up to one bf16 ulp.
+    """
+    residual, layer_input = mhc_post_collapse_rms_norm_triton(
+        residual,
+        sublayer_out,
+        post_layer_mix,
+        comb_res_mix,
+        pre_mix,
+        norm_weight,
+        norm_eps,
+    )
+    main = torch.cuda.current_stream()
+    stream.wait_stream(main)
+    with torch.cuda.stream(stream):
+        post_mix, comb_mix, _, next_pre_mix = (
+            torch.ops.vllm.mhc_fused_post_pre_delayed_rms_norm_aiter(
+                residual,
+                fn,
+                hc_scale,
+                hc_base,
+                rms_eps,
+                hc_pre_eps,
+                hc_sinkhorn_eps,
+                hc_post_mult_value,
+                sinkhorn_repeat,
+                pre_mix,
+                None,
+                None,
+                None,
+                norm_weight,
+                norm_eps,
+                None,
+            )
+        )
+    for tensor in (residual, pre_mix):
+        tensor.record_stream(stream)
+    for tensor in (post_mix, comb_mix, next_pre_mix):
+        tensor.record_stream(main)
+    return residual, post_mix, comb_mix, layer_input, next_pre_mix

**Minor**: is it possible to simplify this a bit by following the structure used in the nvidia/model? I.e.

```
        mhc_pre = (
            partial(mhc_pre_delayed_overlap, stream=mhc_stream)
            if mhc_stream is not None
            else mhc_pre_delayed_tilelang
        )
```

and call mhc_pre unconditionally

**Nit question**: I kind of like the name mhc_pre_delayed_overlap more than mhc_seam_overlap, WDYT?

**Suggestion**: can we check fi we need to register this new kernel for warmup?

 One can run with `--jit-monitor-mode error` to check this

**Question**: can we check if there's a risk we're breaking things given the condition is slightly different from where we sync below (there we just check if the aux stream exists)? I.e. can we get a situation where mhc_stream exist but pre_mix be None? If so we would not run in two streams, but we'd still wait on the aux stream after the ffn

**Question**: I think this will bypass the check of if the aiter mhc kernel is supported by calling it this way (i.e. never checking `_aiter_mhc_supported`). I'm thinking if we should call the MHCPreDelayedOp instead which does this checking for us. Can you check this please?
**Minor**: If we want I think we could re-use enable_multi_stream_overlap utility here

**Optional question**: I might be completely wrong here, but is the norm done in this kernel and the norm done in `mhc_fused_post_pre_delayed_rms_norm_aiter` both on the layer input (i.e. partly redundant) or is it norming different things? Thinking if a natural follow up optimization is to get rid of that if that's the case
**Small question**: What's the reason for 0 absolute tolerance here? I'm thinking if we rather should add a small value if this will always lead to a pass if one of the elements are exactly 0

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

Before approving this, can we either gate the overlap to gfx950 or add gfx942 validation? supports_mhc_overlap() currently enables the path on any ROCm target where the AITER operation is available, but the validation and the 128-token limit are based only on MI355X.
Great work! Can we please do some checks if this also works with dcp and sequence parallel and similar?
